sam: Quick sync - yesterday a dedicated pool hit full allocation during a tenant burst; autoscaler spun up but admission lagged and neighbors saw p95 blips.

jin: Do we know if the lag came from allocator latency or admit surface queuing?

parul: Traces show allocator created pods but kube scheduling + image pull added ~20s. Admit layer kept filling until headroom negative.

sam: Proposal: keep a small always-free headroom (2 GPUs per pool) + prewarm policy for predicted bursts. If headroom exhausted, start per-tenant progressive throttles.

jin: Config idea:
```
pool_defaults:
  reserved_headroom: 2
  prewarm_prediction_window_s: 60
```

parul: We'll need metric reserved_headroom_utilization and prewarm_miss_rate. Also a canary rollout and kill-switch.

ops-bot: alert("headroom-exhaustion") created for canary pool 1769993380

sam: OK. Parul to draft short RFC and small patch to admit filter; jin to prototype prewarm predictor. Close and follow up in PRs.
